alignments.note: Construct noun; supplied indefinite article joins the noun under rule 15.
Article on the rectum; ASV writes no 'the' for the phrase (rule 29).
Rectum takes 'of' under rule 19.
Temporal בְּ + infinitive construct recast as a finite clause takes 'When' (rule 52).
Infinitive construct rendered transitively; 'back' stays with the verb because 'brought' alone does not write the returning (rule 44, as with שׁוּב → 'turn ... again').
Object marker; ASV renders the object bare (rule 16).

The ASV's 'those that returned' answers to a reading of this word as the participle (שָׁבֵי) rather than the noun שִׁיבָה the projection carries; no variant unit is recorded, so under rule 53 the English is aligned to the token as printed. The nominal recast as head noun plus relative clause is one unit (rule 46 closing paragraph), headed on the verb the recasting writes.
Rectum of the chain; the ASV recasts the construct relation with 'to', which belongs to the rectum (rule 19).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
Comparative preposition rendered by a two-word expression; headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 24).
Anarthrous substantival participle takes the supplied 'them that' (rule 46), headed on the lexeme.

review_notes: 'those that returned' (s008) reflects a different reading of שִׁיבַת; no variant unit recorded, aligned as printed under rule 53.

alignments.note: Niphal 'was filled'; the 'with' English needs to reach the bare accusative complement of מָלֵא is the predicate's own under rule 33's מָלֵא clause, and its repetition over the gapped second colon joins the same discontinuous unit under rule 25. Competing reading: give each 'with' to the bare noun (s003, s009) as an adverbial accusative under rule 33's first sentence.
Gapped colon; the verb's 'with' is placed on s002 under rule 25.
Finite verb with its inverted subject pronoun (rule 17).
Assimilated article takes the written 'the' (rule 12).

הִגְדִּיל לַעֲשׂוֹת: the hiphil's whole contribution is the greatness, written by the ASV as 'great' with a supplied generic 'things' (rule 56's auxiliary-verb clause, cf. הִרְבָּה לַעֲשׂוֹת → 'wrought much'; generic joins under rule 31). The finite predicate 'hath done' goes to the infinitive the ASV made the English verb.
לְ before the infinitive left with no English word by the finite recasting (rule 52/40).
Infinitive construct rendered as the clause's English predicate with its auxiliary (rule 56 division).
עִם rendered 'for' (rule 11).
Demonstrative rendered by the pronoun 'them'.

review_notes: 'with' twice placed on the verb s002 (rule 33 מָלֵא clause + rule 25); alternative noted in unit.

alignments.note: As in v.2: the hiphil's contribution is 'great', with supplied generic 'things' (rules 56, 31).
לְ before the infinitive left with no English word (rule 52/40).
Infinitive rendered as the English predicate with its auxiliary.
עִם rendered 'for'.
Supplied connective 'Whereof' (ASV italic); no conjunction or relative morpheme stands in the clause (rules 14, 55).
Written הָיָה takes the copula and subject pronoun (rule 17).
שׁוּב → 'Turn again' keeps 'again' with the verb, since 'turn' alone does not write the returning (rule 44).

Tagged Sh (paragogic/emphatic he on the imperative), not Sd; unrepresented under rule 32's first sentence. The gloss 'back' is a display aid (rule 39). Competing reading: treat as directive he taking 'again'.
Vocative takes the supplied 'O' (rule 36).
Object marker; object rendered bare (rule 16).
Variant WLC.PSA.126.4.v001 underdetermined, r00-base retained; ASV compatible.

review_notes: Variant v001 (s005–s006) underdetermined with r00-base retained; not an excluded fallback, so rule 53 does not apply.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 126:4 'Turn again our captivity' renders the noun with 1cp suffix; qere שְׁבִיתֵנוּ and ketiv שבותנו are orthographic variants of the same word (shebith/shebuth, 'captivity') with identical sense and suffix, so the English cannot distinguish them. No textual note on the verse. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

alignments.note: Substantival article takes the supplied 'They that', headed on the pronoun (rule 41).
Imperfect with its auxiliary (rule 17).

Cognate infinitive absolute expressing emphasis or continuation, with no distinct English rendering: 'forth' states outward motion, not the infinitive's force, so rule 56 does not assign it to this morpheme; the repeated occurrence is unrepresented under rule 22.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun 'He' (rule 17), discontinuous around the supplied relative.

The ASV subordinates a Hebrew main clause as a relative; no relative or article morpheme licenses 'that' (rule 55). Competing reading: 'He that' as a supplied headless-relative noun phrase joining s002 under rule 46.

'goeth' already renders הלך's going; 'forth' supplies an outward direction that no morpheme in this clause writes, so it is added under rule 44. Competing reading: keep 'goeth forth' as the finite verb's phrasal rendering; the separate particle is preferred because its outward direction is additional, not the infinitive absolute's emphasis or continuation.
Infinitive absolute rendered as a finite verb.

Construct מֶשֶׁךְ read by the ASV as 'sowing' (the margin's 'the measure of seed' read and set aside, rule 38); the chain is inverted in English, and the 'for' stands before the construct's own word, so it joins that unit. Competing reading: 'for' to the rectum s008 under rule 19.
Article on the rectum; ASV writes no 'the' (rule 29).
Infinitive absolute takes the intensifier 'doubtless' (rule 56).
Finite verb with its auxiliary; 'again' is not the verb's (see added unit).
'come' already writes בּוֹא's lexeme and 'again' adds a return the Hebrew does not write (rule 44, as 'bring him back').
Supplied preposition and pronoun (ASV italic) with no morpheme for either; one added unit under rules 2 and 33.

review_notes: Margin 'bearing the measure of seed' read and set aside (rule 38).

Scoped TS09 review: s001 has no distinct English rendering and is unrepresented; t004 'forth' is added under rule 44, rather than allocated to the infinitive absolute merely as leftover English. Other constructions were outside this review's scope.
